lines: On the evening of November 11, 1572,
On the evening of November eleventh, fifteen seventy-two,
he spotted a new star in Cassiopeia,
brighter than Venus.
People then believed the heavens never change,
but Tycho measured it night after night,
and found it lay far beyond the Moon:
the sky could change!
The Danish king gave him a whole island, Hven,
where he built an observatory called Uraniborg.
There were no telescopes yet,
so with giant instruments and his bare eyes,
he recorded the positions of the stars
for some twenty years, with amazing precision.

lines: Later, he moved to Prague
and hired a young assistant: Johannes Kepler.
In 1601, Tycho died in Prague, aged fifty-four.
In sixteen oh-one, Tycho died in Prague, aged fifty-four.
His records passed into Kepler's hands,
and after nearly ten years, Kepler found
that the planets move around the Sun in ellipses.
Today, that star is called Tycho's Supernova.
